perf-bot: [ALERT] nightly-ci failed threshold: kv-cache hit-rate drop detected (baseline 82% -> 75%), p95 latency +18% vs baseline for replay harness run. Details: https://dash.redwood.example/perf/1812345678 :warning:

sam: saw this first thing. looks like the KV selector changed in yesterday's kernel-selection patch?

hana: I noticed kernel fallback flags landed in staging, could that change memory layout / cache eviction heuristics?

priya: pushing the nightly logs here — small excerpt of the sampling output:
```
KVCache stats: inserts=1203 evicts=287 hit_rate=0.75
KernelSwitch: selected=fast_attn_v2 fallback=slow_attn
Batching: avg_batch=6.4 max_inflight=12
p95_latency_ms=62.4 p99=120.9
```

miguel: also seeing a higher variance in synthetic load vs replay. replay harness uses longer prefixes (avg 512 tokens) which stresses KV warmup. synth traffic uses many short requests. apples-to-apples might be skewed if harness configs differ.

lena: tagging the nightly job: `nightly/eng-runtime/replay-compare`. ci-bot, can you re-run only the replay harness with debug tracing for this commit range? @ci-bot

ci-bot: Re-run queued: `nightly-replay-debug-1812345678`. Invoked by lena. ETA ~18m. Will upload trace to artifacts when finished. :gear:

sam: thanks. once we have traces let's compare kernel selection histograms and per-request KV hit sequences. If kernel selection heuristics are causing more evictions (smaller KV capacity per shard) that would explain hit-rate drop.

hana: quick theory: the kernel selector changed rounding of sequence-length buckets; that could route medium-length requests to a kernel that uses a different KV allocation strategy. I'll grep the selector diff.

priya: repro command (local):
```
./tools/replay --harness=prod_replay --start=2026-02-01 --end=2026-02-02 \
  --model=redwood-1.2 --quant=fp16 --batch-size=8 \
  --enable-kvcache=true --trace out/trace_1812345678.json
```
Note: include `--prefix-cache=true` to mimic production prefix caching.

miguel: FYI the dashboard shows this spike correlated with a small spike in failed kernel warmups on that host pool (pool-us-west-1b). Could be infra noise. Link: https://dash.redwood.example/infra/hosts/cluster-uswest-1b

sam: action items: 1) compare replay vs synth harness configs to ensure identical prefix lengths and cache toggles, 2) run kernel-selector ablation (old selector vs new) under the replay traffic, 3) add KV cache eviction tracing to nightly replay job so we can see per-shard evict patterns. I'll open a short PR to add eviction traces to the runner.

hana: also let's gate the nightly alert to ignore small infra flaps (hosts with >5% transient errors) to reduce noise. we still want to catch real regressions.

lena: creating an issue for flaky triage: ENGRT-9123. Label: perf, flaky-nightly. Assign to sam + priya.

perf-bot: [INFO] nightly-replay-debug-1812345678 completed. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/artifacts/1812345678/replay-debug.tar.gz

priya: downloaded trace. initial skim: a subset of requests show KV eviction bursts ~200ms before request start, likely due to a background GC task on the same GPU. We should correlate with host logs.

sam: can someone run an apples-to-apples comparison matrix? I want these runs to include: (a) old-kselector + prefix-cache, (b) new-kselector + prefix-cache, (c) new-kselector + no-prefix-cache, all under the same replay set. small script below to launch matrix:
```
for K in old new; do
  ./ci/run_bench --harness=replay --kselector=$K --prefix-cache=true --out=bench_${K}_pc.json
  ./ci/run_bench --harness=replay --kselector=$K --prefix-cache=false --out=bench_${K}_npc.json
done
```

hana: I'll help analyze results and compute p95/p99 deltas and KV hit-rate differences. We should publish a short dashboard tile for the matrix so it's easy to compare.

miguel: recommend adding a flaky-tag mechanism so nightly alerts that flip within 3 runs become lower-priority. we've been chasing infra flaps a lot.

lena: for the triage meeting tomorrow: bring traces and the kernel-selector diff, and the host GC evidence. meeting invite sent to eng-runtime and eng-infra.

sam: one more note — if we confirm kernel selection rounding is the culprit we can add a compatibility layer in the selector to preserve previous bucket boundaries for a rollout window. cheaper than reverting.

perf-bot: [RESOLVED] after matrix runs, regression narrowed to kernel-selector + certain host GC timing. Temporary mitigation: pin kernel-selector to previous version in the nightly compare job. Will follow up with rollout plan. :white_check_mark:

hana: nice, thanks team. summary and next steps in ENGRT-9123.

miguel: marking thread resolved but keeping the issue open until we have the rollout and permanent fix. :+1:
